figure: Figure 3.4 — Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior (caption + in-figure legends)
issue: The caption states the dense 70B has 'resident weights = 140 GB at FP8'. That is arithmetically impossible: 70B parameters at 1 byte/param is 70 GB; 140 GB implies 2 bytes/param (FP16/BF16). The figure's own numbers also mix precisions inside a single comparison: 'inactive experts = 68 GB (6 x 11.4)' and 'active experts = 23 GB resident (2 x 11.4)' imply 11.4 GB per 11.4B-parameter expert = 1 byte/param (FP8), while '= 91 GB experts + 3 GB always-on' implies the 1.4B always-on block is counted at 2 bytes/param, and '= 12.8B = 25.6 GB' implies all active parameters are counted at 2 bytes/param. The headline comparison '140 GB dense vs ~94 GB MoE' is therefore not like-for-like, and the caption's precision label is wrong under every reading.
evidence: Recomputation from the figure's own inputs: 70e9 x 1 B = 70 GB (not 140); 70e9 x 2 B = 140 GB. 8 x 11.4B = 91.2B expert params; 91.2e9 x 1 B = 91.2 GB (matches '91 GB experts'); x 2 B = 182.4 GB (does not match). 1.4e9 x 2 B = 2.8 GB (~'3 GB always-on'); x 1 B = 1.4 GB. 12.8e9 x 2 B = 25.6 GB (matches '= 25.6 GB'); x 1 B = 12.8 GB. Independent cross-check: Figure 5.1 (PDF 110 / printed 90) labels the same canonical model '70B FP16 . serving', consistent with 140 GB = FP16 and contradicting 'at FP8'.
acceptance_test: In the source, fix one precision for the whole comparison and make every printed number follow from it. If FP16 throughout: expert residency becomes 182 GB and the caption's '~47B MoE'/'~27%' must be reconciled with the figure. If FP8 for experts: dense residency becomes 70 GB and the caption must not say '140 GB at FP8'. Acceptance: a reviewer recomputing params x bytes/param reproduces every printed resident figure exactly, and the '= 25.6 GB' active figure uses the same bytes/param as the residency figures.

figure: Figure 3.4 — caption (MoE total parameters and active-compute fraction)

The figure states 8 experts x 11.4B = 91.2B expert parameters plus 1.4B always-on = 92.6B total, which yields an active fraction of 12.8/92.6 = 13.8%, not ~27%. Conversely 12.8/47 = 27.2% is consistent with the caption's ~47B total, which contradicts the figure's 8 x 11.4B. In addition the dense-case fraction renders as '~10^6', which is not a fraction at all (presumably a mis-set '~100%' or a stray superscript). acceptance_test: Verify in source and print exactly one MoE parameter count, one resident-bytes figure, and one active fraction, all derived from the same expert size and layer/head geometry. The dense fraction must print as a percentage (100%) or a ratio (1.0), never '10^6'. figure: FIGURE A.2 — Vendor-relative KV/compute ratios
issue: Unexplained color coding of the model names: 'DeepSeek V4-Flash' is red, 'DeepSeek V4-Pro' is blue, 'GLM-5.3-Flash' is green, with no legend anywhere in the figure or caption. The two rows of the same family (DeepSeek V4) carry different hues, which implies a distinction the figure never defines and that contradicts the figure's own statement that the rows are 'one row per reported model'. In grayscale the three hues collapse to nearly the same mid-gray, so the coding carries no information in print.
evidence: Rendered page 448, first column: 'DeepSeek V4-Flash' in red, 'DeepSeek V4-Pro' in blue, 'GLM-5.3-Flash' in green. No key for these colors appears in the figure, the source line, or the caption.
acceptance_test: Either all model names are set in one color, or the colors encode a defined property (e.g. family) with a legend and a redundant non-color cue (grouping rule, indentation, or family sub-heading). DeepSeek V4-Flash and DeepSeek V4-Pro must not carry different hues unless the difference is defined.

figure: FIGURE A.2 — Vendor-relative KV/compute ratios
issue: Label-scope mismatch between figure and caption. The in-figure source line labels the whole value set 'Value source: vendor-reported [1P]', but the caption splits the same values: '[1P] vendor-reported ratios; [DERIVED] the derived retentions shown in the figure.' The '100% → ~7%' style retentions are derived from reported reductions, so the figure's own label is broader than the caption's and a reader who reads only the figure will treat the derived retentions as first-party reported values.
evidence: Rendered page 448 source line: 'Value source: vendor-reported [1P] — DeepSeek V4: arXiv 2606.19348; GLM: z.ai/blog/glm-5.3-flash (2026-08-26). Vendor claims, not reproduced.' Caption: '[1P] vendor-reported ratios; [DERIVED] the derived retentions shown in the figure.'
acceptance_test: The figure's own source line distinguishes the two provenance classes, e.g. 'vendor-reported [1P] reductions; retentions [DERIVED]'. The figure and caption then assign the same label to the same span.

figure: FIGURE A.2 — Vendor-relative KV/compute ratios
issue: The footnote demonstrates the 'remaining vs reduction' equivalence for one value only ('7% remaining = 93% reduction'), leaving the reader to infer whether the same holds for 10%, 23%, 27% and 33%. The rule is stated once but illustrated once, and the illustrated case is the one most likely to be misread (a 7% figure looks like a typo).
evidence: Rendered page 448 footnote: '*Metric scopes differ. 7% remaining = 93% reduction.'
acceptance_test: The footnote states the rule once for all rows (e.g. 'x% remaining = (100 − x)% reduction; scopes differ — see row labels') or the equivalence is shown for every row.

figure: FIGURE A.2 — Vendor-relative KV/compute ratios
issue: Alignment mismatch: all four column headers are centred while every data cell is left-aligned, so the header-to-cell association is weaker than it needs to be for a table whose whole purpose is a four-column comparison. There are no column rules either, so the reader must rely on whitespace alone.
evidence: Rendered page 448: headers 'reported model | own baseline | KV cache* | Compute*' centred over the column band; row content ('vs V3.2', '100% → ~7%', '100% → ~10%') left-aligned beneath them.
acceptance_test: Each header is aligned with the content of its own column (left-align headers over left-aligned cells, or right-align numeric columns and their headers), and the scan path from header to value is unambiguous at print size.

figure: FIGURE A.4 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
issue: The legend gloss 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs' is inaccurate for the 'Inside post-training' band, which is a development-time activity rather than a runtime location, and the within-hue lightness ramp (dark at the top of each group, light at the bottom) is never explained even though it encodes vertical position. The reader is left to guess what shade depth means.

figure: FIGURE A.4 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
issue: 'Inside post-training' is a development-time activity, not a runtime placement location, so it does not sit on the same axis as the other seven bands ('Inside weights', 'Inside attention', 'Inside MoE routing', 'Inside test-time search', 'Inside tools', 'Inside agent runtime', 'Across a fleet of models'), all of which describe where capability sits while a system is running. figure: FIGURE A.3 — A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems
issue: The bands are drawn as a contiguous, gapless stack, which is the standard visual grammar for a substrate/dependency hierarchy — each layer resting on the one below. The caption disclaims precisely that reading ('the vertical stacking is a layering … not a causal lineage: a later layer does not require the one below it'), but the disclaimer is textual only and the drawing carries the stronger, wrong signal. A reader who skims the figure will retain the dependency reading.
evidence: Rendered page 451: nine bands stacked with no vertical gaps and no separating rules; caption: 'the vertical stacking is a layering (which capabilities sit on which substrate), not a causal lineage: a later layer does not require the one below it, and the eras overlap.'
acceptance_test: The drawing itself carries the non-dependency reading: visible gaps between bands, a left-hand bracket labelled 'capability stack — not a dependency chain', or a legend entry stating 'stacked for display; no layer requires the one below'. A reader who sees only the drawing does not infer a dependency chain.

acceptance_test: All three legend entries begin with a capitalised term and use the book's typographic quotation marks; capitalization within entries is consistent.

figure: Figure 6.2 annotation box vs Section 6.3.1 prose
issue: The figure reports a sample mean of 0.85 s while the prose calls the mean of that same stream 0.84 s; the two quantities are different and the prose conflates them.
evidence: Prose: 'The mean of that stream is ~ 0.99 x 0.8 + 0.01 x 5.0 = 0.84 s'. Figure annotation box: 'mean = 0.85s'. The 0.84 s expression is the two-point approximation; the plotted sample's mean is 0.85 s because the log-normal body is right-skewed and its mean exceeds its median. The prose's phrase 'the mean of that stream' attaches the approximation to the sample.
acceptance_test: Prose must distinguish the two-point approximation (~0.84 s) from the plotted sample mean (0.85 s), or the figure's box must print 0.84 s; the two must not both claim to be 'the mean of that stream'.
